title: Venetian forty-day maritime quarantine
summary: In 1448 the Venetian Senate prolonged a maritime waiting period to forty days, giving rise to the term quarantena.

title: William Henry Duncan's Liverpool sanitary report
summary: Duncan reported on the sanitary state of Liverpool's laboring classes as evidence to Edwin Chadwick's Poor Law Commission inquiry.

title: Duncan's lecture on Liverpool mortality
summary: Duncan presented and published an account of Liverpool's high mortality and its physical causes; the pamphlet moved the town council to act on sanitation.

title: Liverpool Sanitary Act 1846
summary: The local act set minimum housing standards, barred cellar dwellings, and recognized the need for a medical officer to address sanitation.

parents.reason: Duncan's published mortality lecture immediately persuaded Liverpool's council that sanitary action was needed.

title: Metropolis Management Act 1855
summary: Parliament created a London-wide Metropolitan Board of Works to coordinate infrastructure and established parish and district works boards.

title: Metropolitan Board of Works begins operations
summary: The London-wide board took over the powers and duties of the Metropolitan Commission of Sewers and coordinated major public works, including the core sewer system.

parents.reason: The 1855 Act constituted the board, which assumed its powers and duties on 1 January 1856.

title: New York City Department of Health, 1870
wiki: New York City Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
summary: New York replaced its Metropolitan Board of Health with a Department of Health that also assumed street-cleaning and sanitary-permit responsibilities.

title: Biggs directs New York City bacteriology laboratories
summary: From 1892, Hermann Biggs directed New York City bacteriological laboratories, applying bacteriology to infectious-disease prevention and control.

parents.reason: Biggs directed the municipal laboratories as a medical officer of the New York Department of Health.

title: New York City public-school nursing service
summary: Henry Street Settlement funded New York City's first public-school nurse, adapting neighborhood nursing to pupils whose treatable illnesses kept them out of school.

title: U.S. Hygienic Laboratory
summary: The Marine Hospital Service established a bacteriological investigation laboratory at its Staten Island hospital, later moving it to Washington.

title: National Institute of Health, 1930
summary: The Ransdell Act redesignated the Hygienic Laboratory as the National Institute of Health and authorized new buildings for federal biomedical research.

parents.reason: The 1930 institute was the statutory redesignation and expansion of the Hygienic Laboratory.

title: Public Health Laboratory Service
summary: Under the NHS Act, Britain retained and formalized the laboratory network as a national service for communicable-disease surveillance, detection, and control.
